rationale: TWO SPELLINGS, TWO FACTS. `import { alpha as beta }` BINDS `beta` locally — the alias is the local binding (family convention alias||name), and `imports[]` must carry it or the store records a name the file never writes (brain_import.imported_as). The RELATIONSHIP, by contrast, names the symbol in the SOURCE module, which is `alpha`: publishing `beta` as the edge target lets the store's name pass attach the row to any same-named declaration, including one in a different file (measured: an aliased import bound to an unrelated method of the same name). So expectImports pins `beta` and expectRelationships pins `alpha`; the forbid row makes the split falsifiable.

expectRelationships.note: the DECLARED member the edge refers to

forbidRelationships.note: the local binding is not a symbol in the source module
